Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> LivesByProxy wrote:
> Can anyone chime in and comment on the classic weenie Thaumaturgy deck and how that played and wins?
>
I find that the CM deck is quite weak. It can win on a mishap, but if it was "popular" in the 2000s, it's probably more due to a fantasy of playing 15 copies in the same deck and thinking it's going to be great.
Let's not be mistaken: the deck has won a few tournaments, but tournaments of no more than 15 people, and I guess it was in a relaxed atmosphere

Loki's Gift is clearly more interesting. Its attrition power is similar (i.e. low) but it can be played in a more opportunistic strategy by attritioning the right vampire at the right time. I play it for example in a weenie Gangrel vote, and the 2 votes boost allows to get some Praxis that consolidate the number of permanent votes.

Playing both imposes strong constraints on the crypt, for a result no better than playing exclusively CM or LG.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: lip
Messages.Body:
I played CM a bit, I must say Ankha's analysis is on point. A few things you may want to know about the CM archetype (from play experience):  It needs at least 4 vampires, ideally 6+ minions out to be a threat (so weenies, all with ) It needs over 20 copies of CM to be able to take down multiple vampires (30 is not out of question). Society of Leopold helps bring down vampires. Being able to block hunts can also be strong. Vampiric Disease may be good addition depending on the meta (strong against multi-action decks) It bloats with a lot of Vessel/Blood Doll It uses Deflection for defence It bleeds to kill, some Computer Hacking, Govern and/or Conditioning, once your prey does not have the blood anymore to bounce. It is strong against allies Some allies or vampires with CM ability do help (Kyoko, Impundulu, Gregory Winter, Young Bloods) It works best with an even number of players (4 players, duel) because of the stable continuum. So it's stronger in small tournaments with more 4 players tables. If it makes it to the duel, it has a good chance to win.
Still, it is a slow build, the forward power is low, and it takes time to take down a single vampire. More often than not, it just grinds a bit then dies. It needs perfect seating to win. (If the prey is a wall, it dies. If the predators plays politics, it dies. Bloat decks like Girls are crazy hard to take down).

The archetype did win a 41-players tournament in 2002 (UK qualifier): codex-of-the-damned.org/en/deck-search.html?cards=Cryptic+Mission&threshold25=true&id=2k2ukqualifier
Note that 41 players means that had the maximum number of tables of 4 players (4).

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body: I don't see the point in mixing Cryptic Mission with Loki's Gift. It makes your crypt awkward to play 2 cards that are essentially duplicates instead of having synergies. You lose  compared to a normal weenie Tremere and you lose Hunt synergies compared to a dedicated Loki's Gift deck so it looks weaker than either option.
